CHART CODE
 import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

countries = ['Denmark', 'Colombia', 'DR Congo', 'Egypt', 'Cuba']
years = [1960, 1961, 1962, 1963, 1964, 1965]

data = {
    'Denmark': [14500, 14200, 15000, 15800, 16500, 17200],
    'Colombia': [6500, 6800, 7500, 8200, 8900, 9600],
    'DR Congo': [1200, 1300, 1400, 1000, 1100, 1200],
    'Egypt': [1000, 1200, 1300, 1500, 1700, 1900],
    'Cuba': [500, 600, 550, 400, 675, 500]
}

colors = ['#4e79a7', '#f28e2b', '#e15759', '#76b7b2', '#59a14f']

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 7))

for country, color in zip(countries, colors):
    ax.fill_between(years, data[country], color=color, alpha=0.7, label=country)

ax.set_xlabel('Year')
ax.set_ylabel('GDP Growth (%)')
ax.set_title('CO2 Emissions from Solid Fuel Consumption (1960-1965)')
ax.legend(loc='upper left', bbox_to_anchor=(1, 1))
ax.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')

SUMMARY
 This image is an area chart depicting the CO₂ emissions from solid fuel consumption for five countries—Denmark, Colombia, DR Congo, Egypt, and Cuba—over a six-year period from 1960 to 1965. The chart uses distinct colors to represent each country: Denmark is shown in blue, Colombia in orange, DR Congo in red, Egypt in teal, and Cuba in green. The vertical axis measures CO₂ emissions in kilotons (kt), ranging from 0 to 17,500, while the horizontal axis marks the years from 1960 to 1965.

Denmark exhibits the highest emissions throughout the period, starting at 14,500 kt in 1960 and steadily increasing each year to reach 17,200 kt by 1965. Colombia follows as the second-highest emitter, with emissions rising from 6,500 kt in 1960 to 9,600 kt in 1965, showing a consistent upward trend. DR Congo’s emissions, depicted in red, remain relatively low and stable, fluctuating slightly between 1,000 kt and 1,400 kt over the six years. Egypt’s emissions, represented in teal, begin at 1,000 kt in 1960 and gradually increase to 1,900 kt by 1965. Cuba, shown in green, has the lowest emissions, starting at 500 kt in 1960, experiencing minor fluctuations, and ending at the same value of 500 kt in 1965.

The chart effectively highlights the disparity in CO₂ emissions from solid fuel consumption among these countries, with Denmark and Colombia contributing significantly more than the other three nations during this timeframe. The area representation allows for a clear visual comparison of both the magnitude and trends in emissions over the given years.

text = p.read_text()
text = text.replace("'Cuba': [500, 600, 550, 400, 675, 500]", "'Cuba': [500, 600, 550, 400, 450, 500]")

p.write_text(text)
exec(compile(text, "chart.py", "exec"))
import csv
with open("table.csv", newline="") as f:
    rows = list(csv.DictReader(f))
assert years == [int(row["Year"]) for row in rows]
for country in countries:
    assert data[country] == [int(row[country]) for row in rows]
# Check the actual fill geometry as well as the source data.
for collection, country in zip(ax.collections, countries):
    vertices = collection.get_paths()[0].vertices
    for year, value in zip(years, data[country]):
        assert any((vertices[:, 0] == year) & (vertices[:, 1] == value))
assert ax.get_ylabel() == "CO₂ Emissions (kt)"
print("All plotted values match table.csv.")
print("Axis labels:", ax.get_xlabel(), "/", ax.get_ylabel())
print("Title:", ax.get_title())
print("Legend:", ax.get_legend_handles_labels()[1])
